commits.edited_message:
lib: Reserve content model name terminators per scaffold node

build_model() lays out the content model names as each name's characters
followed by a single NUL terminator.  Until now dtd->contentStringLen
conflated the two by counting xcslen(name) + 1 per name, mixing the
character payload with the terminators.

Count only the characters in contentStringLen and reserve the terminators
where the layout actually happens, in build_model(): one extra XML_Char
per scaffold node is a safe upper bound on the number of name nodes.  No
functional change -- the resulting allocation is at least as large as it
was before.

lib: Drop redundant terminator headroom in build_model()

build_model() reserved one extra XML_Char per scaffold node on top of
dtd->contentStringLen to leave room for the content model names' NUL
terminators.  Each name's trailing NUL is already part of the string
payload counted by contentStringLen, so the per-node headroom is dead
space.  Size the string area from contentStringLen alone.

coupling:
Delocalized heap-buffer-overflow (CWE-787) in build_model() reached via XML_Parse() on an internal-DTD element declaration with an element-decl handler registered. build_model() allocates one heap block holding the XML_Content node array followed by a packed list of each content-model name as '<characters><NUL>'. Its size for the string area comes from dtd->contentStringLen.

Commit A (3180710, 'Reserve content model name terminators per scaffold node') silently REDEFINES the meaning of contentStringLen: it stops counting the trailing NUL in the accumulator (nameLen = xcslen(name) instead of xcslen(name)+1 in doProlog's XML_ROLE_CONTENT_ELEMENT case) and compensates by reserving the terminators separately in build_model() as '+ dtd->scaffCount' (a safe upper bound on the number of name nodes). Read alone this commit is net-neutral and correct: the allocation is at least as large as before, so A applied on its own does NOT overflow (verified secure).

Commit B (4d38502, 'Drop redundant terminator headroom in build_model()') removes the '+ dtd->scaffCount' headroom, justified -- plausibly, for a reviewer who only reads B's diff and recalls the ORIGINAL semantics -- by 'each name's trailing NUL is already part of contentStringLen'. That statement was true before commit A but is false after it. Read alone, B's diff looks like a correct cleanup; B's '+ scaffCount' term only exists because of A, so B cannot even be reviewed without A.

Only the COMPOSITION undercounts the string area by one XML_Char per name node: contentStringLen (characters only, from A) with no terminator headroom (removed by B). build_model()'s memcpy() then writes each name's NUL past the end of the allocation -> ASan heap-buffer-overflow. A correct fix must reason across both commits: either restore the per-name +1 in A's accumulator or re-add B's terminator reservation. Fixing either commit's diff in isolation is impossible because neither diff, read on its own, is wrong.
